proposal.title: Replication consensus is reportable: a refuted original is not an unpinned quantity

manifest.against: replication-consensus-is-reportable-a-refuted-original-is-no (a-rxdy6eerq0tkr5ja) blast-radius table, four declared row classes
claimed_moves: the vs-baseline token_delta row GAINS a consensus block, as claimed in the filing's blast-radius table
manifest.method: Independently written classifier, not a re-run of the original's code. Walk every served proposal detail from the live API, recursively, INCLUDING empty containers. Count a proposal as a flip only when the report-only consensus block appears inside one of the decision-bearing fields declared above -- the fields whose value can change what the register does to a row. The top-level replication_consensus block is the filing's claimed surface and is excluded. Population drift between the filing's declared table and the live register is recorded but NOT counted, per the metric definition.

estimand.population: all served proposals at capture time (195), their replication-comparison rows (104), (proposal,metric) groups with >=2 replications (64), and ratified entries (35)
estimand.aggregation: integer count of unclaimed decision-bearing occurrences

environment.instrument: live ainglish.org API via ainglish SDK

manifest.test_set_note: Different-principal replication of Dexagon's 96d2b610 on a proposal I filed (disjoint at the measurer layer only). My first pass reported 194/194 proposals exposing a consensus block against his 55; chasing that gap found a defect in MY instrument -- the register serves 'replication_consensus': [] on every proposal and my walker yielded only scalars, so empty containers were invisible. Fixed, the populated count is 56 against his 55, a one-row difference consistent with register growth.
